text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA

- FPP Oltenia, one of Romania's five regional private ownership funds scheduled to turn into U.S.-style mutual funds, plans to invest in the food industry and the banking sector after its conversion into an investment company.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's long- and medium-term foreign debt rose by $140 million at the end of July.
ADEVARUL
- Medicine prices are expected to rise by 30 percent.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has extended loans worth 52 million Ecus to two brewers in Romania and Croatia.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romania will produces only 70 percent of the 400,000 tonnes of sugar it needs to meet domestic requirements.
ZIUA
- Under a recently adopted government decree, sugar beet imports will be exempt from tax this year.
LIBERTATEA
- Funds worth 600 billion lei were allotted to farmers, who have so far used around 250 billion.
- Romanian privatised companies will be assisted by a recently created post-privatisation fund.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Apollo SA detergent maker will produce Henkel detergents.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes the list of candidates for the parliamentary November 3 elections of the main opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc.

- The case of journalists and members of the December 21 Association of "revolutionaries" accused of forcing their way into a building where a fake telephone poll was allegedly being conducted by the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) will be turned over to the prosecution, police chief Costica Voicu said.
- Over 960 schools need repair works, while another 172 should be closed down for safety reasons in case of an earthquake.
- The newspaper presents in a two-page report on the history of the main opposition Christian Democrat National Peasant Party (PNT-CD), created 70 years ago.
ADEVARUL

- The authorities have lost count of the voters, with a million appearing or disappearing every year, says the newspaper in a front-page report. The electorate over the past six years, it says, ranged from 16.1 to 17.7 million.
- The newspaper publishes the 21 programmes proposed by the ruling PDSR for the November elections.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania registered its first two deaths caused by an overdose of drugs.
- The burglars who broke in the house of the mayor of Bucharest's fifth district took only half of the gold jewellery and money that was there, but showed a considerable interest in documents.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- President Ion Iliescu promulgated the Romanian-Hungarian treaty.
CRONICA ROMANA

- Of the 430 legal actions filed against all 16 presidential candidates, 394 were against President Iliescu, seven against Social Democratic Union candidate Petre Roman and four against CDR candidate Emil Constantinescu. The court rejected them all.
LIBERTATEA

- In a poll asking about the qualities of four presidential candidates, President Iliescu is deemed the most experienced, Petre Roman the sexiest, Gheorghe Funar of the National Unity Party (PUNR) the most patriotic. Emil Constantinescu comes second in most categories. ($=3,268 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
